title: Prescription lock boxes: the definitions in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21B and the sign
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21B(a) defines a lock box as a box with a locking mechanism that cannot be tampered with or opened without extreme force, and a pharmacy as a facility under the direction or supervision of a registered pharmacist which is authorized to dispense controlled substances, provided that pharmacy does not include an institutional pharmacy or a pharmacy department except as otherwise provided in 247 CMR. Under s. 21B(b) a pharmacy registered in the commonwealth to dispense schedule II, III, IV or V prescription drugs shall make available prescription lock boxes for sale at each store location, and pharmacies shall make customers aware of their availability by displaying a sign on or near the pharmacy counter that is at least 4 inches by 5 inches and includes, in legibly printed font, the statement: "Lock boxes for securing your prescription medications are available at this pharmacy".
exam_relevance: Tests the registrant that carries the duty, the store-level availability for sale, and the size, placement and wording of the sign.

numeric_facts.fact: minimum size of the lock box sign
numeric_facts.conditions: displayed on or near the pharmacy counter; M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21B(b)(i)

exceptions: An institutional pharmacy or a pharmacy department is not a pharmacy for s. 21B, except as otherwise provided in 247 CMR.
common_confusions: The statute requires lock boxes to be made available for sale; it does not require them to be given away.
The duty is triggered by registration to dispense Schedule II, III, IV or V prescription drugs, and it attaches at each store location.
verification_notes: Read in full on 2026-09-17 in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21B on malegislature.gov.
